title: The wrong queen
hookLine: Hanuman thinks he's found Sita in Ravana's palace, then knows by her character that he hasn't
carry: sita is known, and honored, by her faithfulness

cards: All night Hanuman has searched Lanka house by house, and every house has been the wrong one. Now he reaches the heart of the city, Ravana's own palace, glittering and guarded, and slips inside.

In the innermost room he sees a woman so beautiful and regal that his heart leaps. After a hundred yojanas of sea and a city full of strangers, he's sure he has found her. He's about to celebrate too soon.

teach.b: Valmiki takes his time getting there. First Hanuman sees the Pushpaka, the flying chariot Ravana took from his half-brother Kubera, covered in jewels and seeming to float.
Then a vast hall where Ravana's many wives lie asleep after a night of music, like a lake of lotuses closed for the night. Then Ravana himself, asleep on a magnificent bed.
And near him, on a separate couch, a woman lovelier than all the rest, adorned and serene.
Hanuman's joy explodes. He slaps his arms, kisses his tail, runs about, sings, climbs the pillars and jumps down again. He's a monkey, and for one moment he acts like one.

teach.h: SITA WOULD NOT SLEEP LIKE THIS.
teach.b: Sita, separated from Rama, would not sleep peacefully. She wouldn't wear jewels, or eat and drink at a banquet. She would never lie content in another man's palace.
This is not Sita. It's Mandodari, Ravana's chief queen. He had only glimpsed Sita once, far off in the sky, as Ravana carried her past.
So he corrects his mistake not by looking harder at a face, but by thinking about who Sita is: her grief, her faithfulness, her love for Rama. He knew her character before he knew her face.
And that character is why Sita is honored in Hindu homes, not only as Rama's wife but as a goddess, whom many see as Lakshmi come to earth.

teach.h: JAI SIYA RAM: HER NAME FIRST.
teach.b: Many devotees greet one another with Jai Siya Ram, victory to Sita and Rama, her name said first.

how: Many devotees greet one another with Jai Siya Ram, Sita's name before Rama's, and readers of the Sundara Kanda smile at Hanuman's leap of joy over Mandodari before he reasons from Sita's character.

games.q: you're Hanuman. you've found a radiant queen asleep in Ravana's inner room. what tells you if she's Sita?
o: whether she'd be sleeping peacefully, jeweled and content, apart from Rama.
how close she is to Ravana.
games.why: Hanuman reasons that grieving, faithful Sita wouldn't sleep, feast or adorn herself in another's palace. this is Mandodari.

practice: Think of Sita the way Hanuman did, by who she is: faithful, grieving, unbending. If you pray, say Siya Ram slowly with the breath, Siya on the way in, Ram on the way out.
If you don't pray, think of someone you love and, instead of their face, call up how they are, one quality on each breath.

wordCard.voice: Ravana's palace. The flying chariot, the hall of sleeping queens, and Mandodari, whom Hanuman mistakes for Sita until he remembers who Sita is.

orig.note: Sanskrit puṣpaka, from puṣpa, flower: the name of the flying chariot.
